To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the terminal RNA structures and their associated sequences are essential for initiation and replication of flavivirus genomes.
the terminal regions of flavivirus genomes contain multiple conserved structures and sequences that function in genome replication, translation and possibly other processes.

the 3' RNA structures and sequences of flaviviruses are involved in multiple steps of the flavivirus replication cycle including initiation of minus strand synthesis, regulation of replication and translation, and possibly regulation of virus release.
In summary, our research is concerned with
determining the functions of the 5' and 3' terminal regions of the genomes of members of genus Flavivirus.
determining the functions of conserved sequences and RNA structures in the 3′ and 5′ terminal regions of the flavivirus genome and the mechanisms of their actions.
understanding how the terminal sequences of flavivirus genomes function in the viral life cycle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 3' conserved sequences and 5' conserved sequences have multiple functions that are virus, virus strain, and host species specific.
the terminal regions of flavivirus genomic RNA contain many functional sequences and structures that are important for virus replication.
the terminal regions contain a variety of conserved RNA sequences and RNA structures with multiple functions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
these regions of the genome RNA have a number of important functions in the virus life cycle.
the terminal sequences and structures have multiple functions in the flavivirus replication cycle and that the functions are not mutually exclusive.
the terminal regions of the flavivirus genome are involved in many of the functions required for a successful infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the terminal regions are multifunctional.
the 3' genome terminal sequences and structures are multifunctional and that they play a central role in the virus life cycle.
the terminal sequences of the flavivirus genome are not just remnants of an ancient RNA but are essential for viral replication and may also play a role in viral pathogenesis.
